A session-based executor can replace this chain at any card boundary if the owner designates one.

Throughput expansion (owner asked for more lanes): lanes E (Python cohort, 9 repositories) and F (.NET cohort, 5) opened in project/lanes/. Rationale: the primary held 13 of the 23 remaining candidates AND the serialized shared-code queue - it was the bottleneck, not the lanes. From now the PRIMARY RUNS NO CANDIDATES: it works shared-code cards only (41+42, 43, 26, 47, F8, F9, 50, 51, 53, 52, 54, 48) while lanes B/C/D/E/F run candidates. Six workers total, within the coordinator plan disjoint-worker discipline (separate worktrees, disjoint repositories, serialized aggregation). Pause order if usage caps hit: lane F first, then E, then B, then D, then C; the primary never pauses (procedure 2b extended). Lane E and F own no platform module - a shared-code defect they find is a PROPOSAL to the primary, never edited in the lane.

Incident and correction, recorded: spawning lane agents with harness worktree isolation set core.bare=true on the PRIMARY checkout git config, which made git refuse every work-tree operation there. Caught immediately by a failing supervisor commit; core.bare unset, HEAD 692f57c and index intact, nothing lost. Root cause: double isolation - loop-prompt-lane.md section 1.1 already has every lane create its own short-path worktree under C:/w/, so harness-level isolation was redundant and its bookkeeping flipped the parent repo bare. Correction: spawn lane agents WITHOUT harness worktree isolation and let the lane prompt create its own, exactly as lanes B/C/D did on 2026-09-06. If any agent in the primary checkout hits a work-tree fatal, the fix is: git config --unset core.bare - a config flag, never repository damage.

P0 card opened, outranks every other shared-code item. Arrival item 40 (e2a1a83, landed 06:50 today) pins reconciliation_schema fact_ids by regex on an array with no maxItems; under strict json_schema the bare kind prefix satisfies the pattern, so the decoder emits prefixes until the 32000-token budget is gone (finish_reason length), and samples that do complete carry fact_ids that name no fact. S4 runs for every repository: no candidate in any cohort can seal until this lands - this is why the count has not moved. Corroborated independently within one hour by lane D on Go (3bc7999, PROPOSAL P23) and lane C on both Java repositories (852047a, PROPOSAL S), each with measured token counts and a replayed request. Fix direction: pin fact_ids to an enum of the packet real fact IDs, exactly as the same function already does for unit_ids (lane D measured finish_reason stop, 3560 tokens, all 40 dispositions). Fallback: pattern + .+ with maxItems 72 (lane C). Second fallback: revert e2a1a83. Mutation test required: a schema admitting a bare kind prefix must fail.

Lanes B, E and F told to stop candidate runs and record findings only until S4-REGRESSION lands - a disposition written against a known-broken stage is a false failure class. Lanes C and D are landing their findings by PR. All five re-spawn once the fix is green. Second defect found while reading lane branches: a test fixture committed into the surrounding repository - lane branches carried 8 and 16 commits by author Test (seed/initial/placeholder, aspose scaffolding) on top of real lane work, because a fixture git command ran without its own repo and walked up to the worktree git dir. Both lanes told to reset to their real commit before opening a PR; a squash-merge would otherwise have carried fixture scaffolding onto main. Candidate arrival item when a lane names the fixture.

Until run_git stops forwarding GIT_DIR, this checkout config is poisoned repeatedly by the test fixtures: user.name/user.email were rewritten to Test/test@example.com twice within ten minutes (two commits already on main carry it, section 31 13:52) and core.bare was flipped to true twice, each time making every git work-tree operation fail with <fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree>. Working practice for every agent until the fix lands: (1) commit with an explicit identity override rather than trusting config - git -c user.name="Babar Raza" -c user.email="babar.raza@aspose.com" commit ... - it is immune to config poisoning; (2) if a git command fails with the work-tree fatal, run git config --unset core.bare and continue, it is a flag not damage; (3) check git log -1 authorship after committing. The pre-push hook path is already closed (9fe49e0 scrubs the GIT_* family before running ci_check.sh), so a hook-driven suite no longer pollutes; direct pytest runs in a shell that already has GIT_DIR set still can.

Capacity fact, recorded: all six workers (primary + lanes B/C/D/E/F) hit the account session limit SIMULTANEOUSLY at 3:20pm Karachi reset - confirming the cap is account-wide, not per-agent, and six concurrent opus workers exhausts it together rather than one at a time in the recorded pause order (F, E, B, D, C). Reset passed at ~15:24; all five stopped agents resumed with context intact via SendMessage at their exact cutoff point - no work lost, uncommitted candidate bundles verified intact on disk first. Real signal recovered from the cutoffs: lane B reached genuine ACCEPTED / verdict ACCEPT / second_reader.read 2 on aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp before the cut - the corroboration guard (PHASE1/F6) held on its first live candidate. No-op proof was in progress when the limit hit; lane B resumed to finish it. Working practice: six concurrent opus lane spawns is the sprint design and stays the design, but a future simultaneous-cutoff should be handled the same way - verify each worktree bundle state on disk before resuming (state/verdict/second_reader fields), never respawn fresh when a resumable agent id exists, since a fresh spawn re-derives measurements that already exist.

FIRST NEW SEAL of the sprint: aspose-cells-foss/Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Go, PR #42 (6045141), BC-01..11 all PASS, review ACCEPT/second_reader.read 2, no-op proof verified by direct sha256 of all 14 bundle files across two independent runs (14/14 unchanged). status now 9/34; 7 current-code reproducible, 1 independently accepted. This confirms 22c2e45 (item 60/61 fix) closes the re-judge-without-call_schema class for EVERY job carrying a call_schema, not S4 alone - lane D measured its own request digest reusing cleanly with zero provider calls on the second attempt. Re-seals for Cells-Java, PDF-Cpp, Email-Cpp and Cells-Python are in flight on the same fix; expect several more seals shortly if their own blockers were genuinely this class. Also recorded: the pre-push hook costs ~10 extra minutes per lane push (serial pytest, 598s, vs 116s for -n auto) - a known cost, not a new defect, tracked as acceptable given the hook is the CI-equivalence guarantee.

Incident: the primary went idle 1h44m (18:33->20:17) after its 60/61 completion report - the supervisor got absorbed in lane re-seals and admitting items 62-64 and forgot to respawn the next card. No automatic re-spawn exists for the primary as a spawned-agent chain (unlike a self-scheduling session, a spawned agent run genuinely ends when it reports; nothing wakes the supervisor to respawn it except the supervisor noticing). Correction: every completion notification for the primary MUST be answered with either a respawn on the next card or an explicit, recorded reason to pause (checkpoint, cap, deliberate hold) - never silently absorbed into other work.
